notes.text: Artemi Panarin is away for personal reasons and has missed the last 2 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Alex Turcotte has taken his spot beside Adrian Kempe and Alex Laferriere.
Trevor Moore is out, reported after he played in their last game.
Erik Gustafsson returned in their last game after missing 3 games. Their recent numbers were built mostly without him.

Kirill Marchenko is out week to week (lower body injury) and has missed the last 9 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Easton Cowan has taken his spot beside Jack Roslovic and Auston Matthews. That line has had 49% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 74:27 together, down from 72% with Marchenko.

Nick Blankenburg is out week to week (upper body injury) and has missed the last 11 games. He is one of their more valuable skaters. Troy Stecher has taken his spot beside Oliver Ekman-Larsson. That pair has had 59% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 61:32 together, up from 48% with Blankenburg.
Morgan Rielly returned in their last game after missing 4 games. Their recent numbers were built mostly without him.
Ryan Tverberg was added to the roster on Nov 12 and has played beside John Tavares and William Nylander.
Oliver Ekman-Larsson has started killing penalties: on the ice for 30% of the team’s shorthanded time in 23 games, up from 6% last season.

stakes: The Kings go in seventh in the Pacific with 14 points, the Maple Leafs eighth in the Atlantic with 18 points.

TOR.head: Not an easy night for the Maple Leafs
TOR.body: Even though Toronto has home-ice advantage and Los Angeles will be without Panarin, the Kings have been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. On top of that, Toronto will be without Marchenko. The Maple Leafs’ best way through is keeping dangerous shots away.

story.head: Something has to change for the Maple Leafs
paras: The Maple Leafs are on a seven-game losing streak, while the Kings (6-11-2) beat Boston 3-0 on Tuesday. Both teams are near the bottom of the standings. Going in, the Kings are seventh in the Pacific (tied for 29th in the NHL) and the Leafs last in the Atlantic (27th).

The Kings have played better than their record (.368) says: their chances are worth about .618, and their finishing has held them back. So have the Maple Leafs (.391 on chances worth .479), mostly because they’re 3-8 in one-goal games.

The Kings keep dangerous shots away better than anyone (1st), leave the shooting to their forwards (2nd lowest) and hound the puck on the forecheck (3rd). On the other side, the Maple Leafs get their shots through better than anyone (1st), but take more penalties than they draw (31st) and have had shaky goaltending (31st). The Kings are likely to get plenty of pucks to the net against the Maple Leafs. Beyond that, the Kings hit a lot, but the Maple Leafs mostly don’t.

Brandt Clarke (3 G / 11 A / 14 P in 19 GP) leads the Kings in scoring, and Adrian Kempe (6 G / 7 A / 13 P in 18 GP) has a team-high six goals. Auston Matthews (12 G / 18 A / 30 P in 23 GP) leads the Maple Leafs in scoring and is tied for seventh in the NHL, and William Nylander (11 G / 11 A / 22 P in 23 GP) isn’t far behind.
Darcy Kuemper (6-5-1 / .884 SV% in 12 GS) is expected to start for Los Angeles, and Anthony Stolarz (5-4-0 / .905 SV% in 9 GS) for Toronto.
